text.p: Dr. Jack Kevorkian dropped off the body of a 65-year-old woman at a hospital on Wednesday night, the 44th time the assisted suicide advocate has admitted helping someone die.

Barbara Collins of Falmouth, Massachusetts, was pronounced dead by William Beaumont Hospital emergency room workers shortly before 8 p.m. EDT (2400 GMT) on Wednesday, said Colette Stimmell, a spokeswoman for the hospital in Royal Oak, a suburb northwest of Detroit.
Kevorkian handed hospital workers a piece of paper with Collins' name, city and a diagnosis of ovarian cancer written on it, Stimmell said.
Following hospital policy, Stimmell said workers called police, who arrived about the time Kevorkian was leaving. Kevorkian spoke with the officers and left some time later.
A spokesman for the Royal Oak Police Department refused to comment on the incident, but said Kevorkian had not been arrested.
Collins' body was transferred to the Oakland County Medical Examiner's office. An autopsy will be performed later Thursday.

Last week, Kevorkian's attorney, Geoffrey Fieger, accused police of illegally tracking the retired pathologist after they interrupted a counselling session between him and a patient who later died in his presence.
The 55-year-old woman, Nancy DeSoto of Bourbonnais, Illinois, was a florist who suffered from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, known as Lou Gehrig's disease, which left her paralysed in a wheelchair.
